operation.$comment: Review 2026-08-22 [P1] on W4487: `signature_digest` is NOT the body digest. Section 4.2 fixes the payload exactly -- the canonical digest of {"kind": <envelope kind>, "operands": <durable body operands>} -- so the operation kind is inside the identity and two kinds carrying identical operands are different operations. A `claim_token` operand enters that payload as its verifier digest, never literally, because a signature is durable and section 13 keeps the bearer off durable surfaces. Transport correlation, `sent_at`, `sender` and `extensions` are excluded. Schema can only prove the digest's SHAPE; section 12 rule 9 states the recomputation, which a receiver of a command performs before journalling the operation. A reply echoes its request's signature and is not recomputed. See work/records/2026/08/finding-worker-control-decline-token-conflict/.

offerDecideBody.$comment: W4487, ruled 2026-08-22: `claim_token` is null for a decline and a string for an accept, and that asymmetry is DELIBERATE. W151 1-ruled section 7 originally required a declining worker to present the exact unspent bearer, which this schema mechanically rejects; the approver kept this non-secret decline envelope and superseded that requirement. A decline is authorized instead by the exact binding of offer_id, runtime_attempt_id, work_ref, decision and reason under the envelope's body_digest, and the manager consumes the offer verifier without a bearer ever being transmitted. Schema proves the shape only; section 12 rule 14 states the binding check no schema can express. See work/records/2026/08/finding-worker-control-decline-token-conflict/.
